title: Model enlistment: automated pinning + publishable profile for embedding->reranker chains
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Goal: Create an automated pipeline that takes a candidate embedding model and downstream reranker, runs deterministic micro-benchmarks and synthetic workload validations, and produces a version-pinned artifact with a published performance profile suitable for Redwood Catalog. The pipeline should: 1) run cross-arch quantized verification (float32 -> int8/4) for embedding accuracy degradation bounds; 2) measure pairing metrics (recall@k, nDCG, latency p50/p95) across canonical prompt sets; 3) produce a pin manifest that includes kernel selection hints, preferred batching windows, KV cache warmup guidance, and a stability score; 4) publish the profile to the catalog with semantic metadata and a human-readable summary for PMs and Solutions Engineering; 5) provide an automated rollback suggestion when a future candidate deviates beyond thresholds.

Why this work: Current onboarding is manual and diverging teams encode ad-hoc steps in PRs. We repeatedly see regressions due to quantization differences and subtle reranker embedding distribution shifts. A single reproducible pipeline will reduce time-to-publish, lower human error, and enable safer canary rollouts on Dedicated and Private deployments.

Non-goals: Full model training, end-user-facing catalog UI changes (console UX will consume profile via API), or making new model selection heuristics for runtime routing (those are separate follow-ups).

Acceptance criteria:
- Pipeline triggered by GH tag or upload generates a pin manifest JSON with fields: model_key, model_hash, quantization_profile, pairing_metrics, kernel_hints, batching_recommendation, stability_score, publishable_summary.
- Automated check runs in <= 90 minutes for 7B-class models on our standard verification infra (two node pool: cpu controller + one GPU worker).
- CI gates fail if embedding retrieval recall drops > 2% absolute or reranker nDCG@10 degrades >4% relative to baseline.
- Profile published to catalog endpoint with a human-readable summary and a test-level provenance link.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Add a new onboarding job to onboarding-ci that accepts model artifact tarball and candidate reranker config.
2) Reuse existing eval harness for canonical prompt sets; extend harness to compute pairing metrics and to replay representative KV lengths for cache-effect measurement.
3) Integrate quantization verification steps invoking quant-test binary; capture per-layer activation shift heuristics in profile.
4) Produce pin manifest and upload to catalog-svc via authenticated publish endpoint.  Include a generated summary.md stored in artifacts storage with links to perf dashboards.
5) Wire a post-publish notification to #model-onboards Slack and create a lightweight ChangeLog PR for catalog content reviewers.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Time vs thoroughness: Running extensive evals with real datasets increases confidence but adds to runtime. We'll start with smaller canonical sets and add optional extended runs for heavy-weight models.
- Resource constraints: Current verification pool has limited GPU slots; we will queue by priority and provide an opt-in "fast pass" for priority enterprise candidates.
- Determinism: Some metrics (e.g., recall at small k) vary with RNG and tokenization. We'll seed RNGs and fix tokenizers, but still provide a stability score and repeatability checklist.

Risks:
- False negatives: A model may pass synthetic tests but fail on customer workloads. Mitigation: provide a clearly documented canary checklist and sample traffic replay utility for Solutions Engineering.
- Cross-arch quantization surprises: Int4 quantization can change embedding geometry; require explicit quantization delta report in manifest.

Notes on output format: The pin manifest must be machine-parseable but concise; the summary must be friendly to non-engineers and include a one-paragraph TL;DR, key numbers, and recommended runtime knobs.
comments: 2025-02-10 Liam O'Connor: Initial spike complete. Proved we can produce pairing-metrics in the harness with small canonical set. Github sandbox PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/onboarding-ci/pull/512

2025-02-14 Aisha Martinez: Design review with PMs and Solutions Engineering. They asked for an extra field in summary: "recommended_fallbacks" to suggest compatible lighter-weight models on downgrade. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-18 Engineering review: Decided to implement a two-tier run: 'quick' (30-60m) and 'full' (~4h). Quick run will be default for PRs; full run is gated on release candidates. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/emb-rerank-onboard-design
2025-02-21 QA: Found nondeterminism in the tokenization step that affected recall@5. Patch to pin tokenizer version applied in PR #529.
2025-02-24 Security: Quick check completed. No secrets leaked. KMS-access for publishing only available to onboarding-ci-service account. Recorded in security ticket SEC-1987.

2025-02-27 Performance: Benchmark runs for a 7B float->int8 conversion showed embedding cosine mean shift 0.6% and runtime p95 improved by 1.8x. Attached perf dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/emb-onboard/ENG-71109

2025-03-01 Liam O'Connor: Wire-up to catalog-publish endpoint working in staging. Manual publish performed for test candidate 'enc-lite-v2'. Manifest: s3://onboard-artifacts/ENG-71109/enc-lite-v2-manifest.json
